item.title: Renoir 1.12.0
item.description:
Edit states on the canvas, find anything in a drawing, and leave review comments.

  • Move components on the canvas. Drag a component onto another container to move it, in the state on screen for a drawing with states. Right-click for Move To, Remove from this state, Gone After, New in, and Keep in Every State. Each change previews a fresh layout for Save Version, and Edit › Undo (⌘Z) takes it back.
  • Find in the drawing. Edit › Find in Drawing (⌘F) highlights every component whose name, description, or details match and zooms to each in turn; ⌘G and ⇧⌘G step through them. Search Library is now ⌥⌘F.
  • Review comments. Comment on a component or the whole drawing from the inspector's Comments tab, by right-clicking, or with Drawing › Add Comment (⇧⌘K). Components with open comments get a marker on the canvas. Comments don't make saves and never appear in exports, and your AI client can read and resolve them with the new list_comments, add_comment, resolve_comment, and delete_comment tools.

Renoir 1.11.0 and later update themselves; choose Renoir › Check for Updates… to get this version now. From earlier versions, download the DMG, open it, and drag Renoir.app to Applications. The MCP helper is inside the app at Renoir.app/Contents/MacOS/RenoirMCP; see MCP setup for client configuration.

Requires macOS 14 or newer. The build is ad hoc signed and has not been notarized by Apple, so macOS may ask you to approve its first launch.

item.title: Renoir 1.11.0
item.description:
Renoir now keeps itself up to date.

  • Automatic updates. Renoir checks for new versions and installs them for you. Choose Renoir › Check for Updates… to check now, and turn automatic checks and installs on or off in Settings › General, which also shows the version you have.
  • Signed and checked. Updates come from Renoir's public releases at acousland/Renoir-releases, and Renoir installs one only if it's signed with Renoir's own key.
  • This is the last version to install by hand. Once you have it, later versions arrive on their own.

Download the DMG, open it, and drag Renoir.app to Applications. The MCP helper is inside the app at Renoir.app/Contents/MacOS/RenoirMCP; see MCP setup for client configuration.

Requires macOS 14 or newer. The build is ad hoc signed and has not been notarized by Apple, so macOS may ask you to approve its first launch.
